title: When the picture store is full, a gym owner is told the logo is over 1 MB
what: The logo upload turns any failure whose message holds words like 'exceeded' or 'size' into 'That logo is over 1 MB. Pick a smaller one.' The logo is already shrunk and checked to be under 1 MB before upload, so the likely cause of such a failure is the picture store's plan limit, not the file. The owner keeps trying smaller logos that can never work, and nobody at MettleUp is told.
expected: A failure from a full picture store tells the owner it is our problem and to message MettleUp, and MettleUp gets a warning before the store fills up.
how_often: only once the picture store reaches its plan limit
fix_line: Tell a storage-full failure apart from a too-big file and show plain words that point to MettleUp

items.reason: Paid or capped things here: Supabase picture storage (gym-logos bucket, 1 MB per file, Free 1 GB total) and its download traffic. Background removal and colour suggestion run in the browser, so no AI or paid call. Every upload is a new file never deleted, so storage grows with no per-gym cap (existing findings).
Upload ticket limit gives clear 'too many uploads' words; a full picture store is misreported as a too-big logo. Size of the bucket today: unknown (machine file could not measure it).
No usage warning for picture storage or its download traffic in this area; the same gap is already recorded for HQ.
